catalog_quote: There is also a reduced presyllable Cə which can occur in unstressed initial CV syllables. e.g. [ʔə³.mɔu³⁵] ‘feather’, [ŋə³.laŋ³] ‘forehead’. [p. 6] ... One final vowel process is vowel reduction to a [ə] which can occur in word initial, unstressed, open syllables as represented in (16). (16) vowel ---> ə in an open, unstressed, word initial CV syllable. There is not sufficient data to determine exactly which vowels will reduce in word initial unstressed syllables, but some examples are indicated below (17). (17) wu³ ‘bamboo’ vs. wə³.mjɨk³ ‘bamboo shoot’ / dzɨ⁴ ‘tooth’ vs. dzə⁵⁴.gok⁵³ ‘gums’ / nʉ³ ‘buffalo’ vs. nə³.lɨ³ ‘buffalo’ [p. 12] ... Lashi has three phonemic tones (high-fall, high-mid, low) in open or nasal final syllables. ... There are two tones in checked syllables as shown in (22). ... Tone in reduced syllables is non-contrastive and tends to assimilate to the tone of the following syllable as shown in (23). (23) dzə⁵⁴.gok⁵³ ‘gums’ / dzə³.lu³ ‘tiger’ / ʔə³.ba³⁴ ‘father’ (vocative) / ʔə⁵.pʰuʔ⁵⁴ ‘father’ (vocative). Exceptions to assimilation are rare but can occur when a voiceless consonant occurs between the two vowels e.g. jə³.tʰoŋ⁵ ‘farm’. [p. 14] ... This analysis posits three contrastive tones in unchecked syllables, high-fall (5-3), high-mid (4), low (2), and two tones in checked syllables, high (4) and low (2). All tones show considerable contour variations. Reduced syllables do not carry contrastive tone. [p. 18]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Lacid/Lashi is a tone language (three contrastive tones in open/nasal-final syllables, two in checked syllables, plus a stiff/slack voice-quality contrast); the source posits no word-stress contrast and gives no positional stress rule. The only stress statement is that in (mostly bisyllabic) words the word-initial CV syllable can be unstressed, in which case its vowel reduces to [ə] and it loses contrastive tone, taking its pitch from the following syllable — i.e. the sesquisyllabic pattern with prominence on the final (major) syllable, the initial minor syllable being unstressed.
new_statements.exceptions: Reduced-syllable tone assimilation can fail when a voiceless consonant intervenes (e.g. jə³.tʰoŋ⁵ ‘farm’). Which vowels reduce in unstressed initial syllables is undetermined ('not sufficient data'). Wannemacher's own list of areas for further study includes 'the initial unstressed CV syllable' (p. 19). Second-hand (Morse 1960 ms., reported on p. 5): on /ʔ/-final syllables 'words with stress' carry high tone and 'unstressed words' low tone.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical word (citation forms elicited in isolation and in a tone frame from a 756-item wordlist; mono-/bisyllabic words and compounds up to four syllables). No phrase-level or intonational stress described.
new_statements.identity_note: Wannemacher 2011 describes the Lacid of the Waimo area, eastern Kachin State, Myanmar (three male speakers, 1994); Luk 2017 describes Myanmar Lacid (thesis supported by the Lacid Language and Culture Committee). Glottolog has no dialect-level codes under lash1243; the Chinese-side variety is called Leqi (勒期语) in Dai's works. No differently named variety is involved.

tone_statements.quote: This paper will examine the phonological and grammatical differences below between the standard Cang Moo Khung (CMK) variety of ‘Lacid’ in Myanmar and ‘Leqi’ in China. • Rhymes: PTB/PLB *-ə𝘺 corresponds to -𝘪𝘵 in CMK Lacid and -𝘦𝘪 in Leqi, and PTB/PLB *-ə𝘸 corresponds to -𝘢𝘶𝘬 in CMK Lacid and -𝘰𝘶 in Leqi. • Tones: In Leqi, the pitch rise occurred in most syllables with the ‘plain’ initial corresponding to *Tone I syllables in OB, unlike Lacid.
tone_statements.locator: author's abstract (KURENAI item 2433/289965 dc.description.abstract = CiNii crid 2120307889984447744 description); body pp. 33-54 not
tone_statements.summary: Lexical-tone language (per catalog: 3 tones in live syllables, 2 in checked, plus stiff/slack register); this paper adds a cross-variety difference: Leqi (China) shows a pitch rise (tone split/raising) in plain-initial reflexes of OB Tone-I syllables that CMK Lacid (Myanmar) lacks.
